en: (1) The Inevitable Reality -
(2) What is the Inevitable Reality?
(3) And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality?
(4) Thamūd and ʿAad denied the Striking Calamity [i.e., the Resurrection].
(5) So as for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overpowering [blast].

ar: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
en: (6) And as for ʿAad, they were destroyed by a screaming,[1737] violent wind
tr: Waʾammā ʿādun faʾuhlikū birīḥin ṣarṣarin ʿātiyah

ar: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
en: (7) Which He [i.e., Allāh] imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.
tr: Sakhkharahā ʿalayhim sabʿa layāliw wathamāniyata ayyāmin ḥusūman fataral-qawma fīhā ṣarʿā kaʾannahum aʿjāzu nakhlin khāwiyah

en: (8) Then do you see of them any remains?

ar: وَجَآءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَٰتُ بِٱلْخَاطِئَةِ
en: (9) And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities[1738] with sin.
enNotes: [1738]- Those to which Lot was sent (see 11:82-83) or generally, all cities which were destroyed due to their denial of a messenger from Allāh.
tr: Wajāʾa firʿawnu waman qablahū wal-muʾtafikātu bil-khāṭiʾah

ar: فَعَصَوْا۟ رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
en: (10) And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizure exceeding [in severity].
tr: Faʿaṣaw rasūla rabbihim faʾakhadhahum akhdhatar rābiyah

ar: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ حَمَلْنَٰكُمْ فِى ٱلْجَارِيَةِ
en: (11) Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you [i.e., your ancestors] in the sailing ship[1739]

ar: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ
en: (12) That We might make it for you a reminder and [that] a conscious ear would be conscious of it.
tr: Linajʿalahā lakum tadhkirataw wataʿiyahā udhunuw wāʿiyah

ar: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَٰحِدَةٌ
en: (13) Then when the Horn is blown with one blast

ar: وَحُمِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَٰحِدَةً
en: (14) And the earth and the mountains are lifted and leveled with one blow [i.e., stroke] -
(15) Then on that Day, the Occurrence [i.e., Resurrection] will occur,
(16) And the heaven will split [open], for that Day it is infirm.[1740]

ar: وَٱلْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرْجَآئِهَا وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَٰنِيَةٌ
en: (17) And the angels are at its edges. And there will bear the Throne of your Lord above them, that Day, eight [of them].
tr: Wal-malaku ʿalā arjāʾihā, wayaḥmilu ʿarsha rabbika fawqahum yawmaʾidhin thamāniyah

ar: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
en: (18) That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgement]; not hidden among you is anything concealed.[1741]
enNotes: [1741]- i.e., any person or any secret you might attempt to conceal.
tr: Yawmaʾidhin tuʿraḍūna lā takhfā minkum khāfiyah

ar: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقْرَءُوا۟ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
en: (19) So as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!
tr: Faʾammā man ūtiya kitābahū biyamīnihī fayaqūlu hāʾumuqraʾū kitābiyah

en: (20) Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account."
(21) So he will be in a pleasant life -
(22) In an elevated garden,
(23) Its [fruit] to be picked hanging near.

ar: كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَيَّامِ ٱلْخَالِيَةِ
en: (24) [They will be told], "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth[1742] in the days past."
enNotes: [1742]- Literally, "advanced" in anticipation of reward in the Hereafter.
tr: Kulū washrabū hanīʾam bimā aslaftum fil-ayyāmil-khāliyah

ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهْ
en: (25) But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record
tr: Waʾammā man ūtiya kitābahū bishimālihī fayaqūlu yālaytanī lam ūta kitābiyah

en: (26) And had not known what is my account.
(27) I wish it [i.e., my death] had been the decisive one.[1743]
enNotes: [1743]- i.e., ending life rather than being the gateway to eternal life.

en: (28) My wealth has not availed me.
(29) Gone from me is my authority."[1744]
enNotes: [1744]- i.e., I have no valid excuse to stand on.

en: (30) [Allāh will say], "Seize him and shackle him.
(31) Then into Hellfire drive him.

ar: ثُمَّ فِى سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَٱسْلُكُوهُ
en: (32) Then into a chain whose length is seventy cubits insert him."
tr: Thumma fī silsilatin dharʿuhā sabʿūna dhirāʿan faslukūh

ar: إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
en: (33) Indeed, he did not used to believe in Allāh, the Most Great,
(34) Nor did he encourage the feeding of the poor.
(35) So there is not for him here this Day any devoted friend
(36) Nor any food except from the discharge of wounds;
(37) None will eat it except the sinners.
(38) So I swear by what you see
(39) And what you do not see
(40) [That] indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the word of a noble Messenger.

ar: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
en: (41) And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe.
tr: Wamā huwa biqawli shāʿir, qalīlam mā tuʾminūn

ar: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
en: (42) Nor the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.
tr: Walā biqawli kāhin, qalīlam mā tadhakkarūn

en: (43) [It is] a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
(44) And if he [i.e., Muḥammad] had made up about Us some [false] sayings,
(45) We would have seized him by the right hand;[1745]
enNotes: [1745]- Another interpretation is "by [Our] right hand," i.e., Allāh would have exacted revenge with might and power.

en: (46) Then We would have cut from him the aorta.[1746]

ar: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ
en: (47) And there is no one of you who could prevent [Us] from him.
tr: Famā minkum min aḥadin ʿanhu ḥājizīn

en: (48) And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is a reminder for the righteous.
(49) And indeed, We know that among you are deniers.
(50) And indeed, it will be [a cause of] regret upon the disbelievers.
(51) And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
(52) So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
